subject: swampTroll
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: swamp troll with tusks, mohawk and bone fetishes.
Style: Blizzard/Warcraft.
reasoning:
Looking at the renders, I'm trying to pinpoint the most important fixes needed. The head seems off — small, oddly oriented, with the face looking tilted or messy from the front, and the tusks/mohawk placement reading strangely from the side and three-quarter angles.

The troll's posture feels stiff rather than hunched, and the eyes are too small — mostly fine but worth noting. I also spot the back loincloth flap sticking out diagonally in an unnatural way; I'm adjusting its orientation vector so it hangs straighter instead of flaring outward. The fire's flame color also looks too pink/salmon rather than a proper fire glow, which needs correcting.

The cauldron placement and fire positioning look fine, and the floating bone/wisp details seem intentional. My main concerns are the mohawk reading as too thin from the front, the head looking a bit small, and the eyes being too tiny — those need widening and enlarging.

I'm checking the eye decal size and position relative to the brow capsule, deciding to enlarge them for better visibility under the brow shadow. The head-to-shoulder proportions seem acceptable for a troll aesthetic, though I'm considering whether the ears need further enlarging despite already being quite big.

The hunched posture looks decent in three-quarter view, but pushing the spine-to-head offset further feels risky given how many coordinates would need adjusting, so I'll leave it. I'm also reviewing how the totem lantern and torso blobs overlap in the three-quarter view, confirming the positioning looks reasonable despite some visual oddities.

Now I'm tweaking the swamp base details — adding a glowing water pool, improving the fire effect with a light ring, and widening the mohawk spikes by adjusting their offset and direction for a bigger sideways spread.

I'm also enlarging the tusks and raising their tip, boosting eye glow intensity, and refining the fire cone colors, back flap tilt, and overall ember glow strength before finalizing these edits.

Pinpointing unique multi-line snippets around the sides/color parameters to target each glow-strength replacement precisely...

I'm also adjusting the flap's y-direction vector to remove the dirZ tilt and bumping up the eye size dimensions and scale factor.

Now I'm widening the mohawk spike geometry and enlarging the tusk bezier curve path and radius to make them more prominent.
